mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Parseval's identity for Fourier transforms states that:}\)

\(\text{Given the Fourier transform pair } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1-|x|, & |x| \leq 1 \\ 0, & |x| > 1 \end{cases}, F(s) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left( \frac{\sin(s/2)}{s} \right)^2, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t}{t} \right)^4 dt.\)
\(\text{If } f(x) = e^{-a|x|} \text{ and } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{a}{s^2+a^2}, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+a^2)^2}.\)

\(\text{Using Parseval's identity and the Fourier transform of the rectangular pulse } f(x) = \begin{cases} 1, & |x| \leq a \\ 0, & |x| > a \end{cases}, \text{ prove that } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t}{t} \right)^2 dt = \frac{\pi}{2}. \text{ What is the value of } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin(at)}{t} \right)^2 dt?\)

\(\text{For the function } f(x) = \begin{cases} a^2-x^2, & |x| \leq a \\ 0, & |x| > a \end{cases} \text{ with Fourier transform } F(s) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left( \frac{\sin(as)-as\cos(as)}{s^3} \right), \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \left( \frac{\sin t - t\cos t}{t^3} \right)^2 dt.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Identity: } \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |F(s)|^2 ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Proof: Start from convolution theorem with } g(x) = \overline{f(-x)}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Then } F[g] = \overline{F(s)} \text{ and } (f*g)(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t) \overline{f(t)} dt\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Also, } (f*g)(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) \overline{F(s)} ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Equating gives the identity.}\)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State and prove Parseval's identity for Fourier transforms.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Take } f(x)=e^{-|x|}, \text{ then } F(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Parseval: } \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-2|x|} dx = 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-2x} dx = 1\)

(2 Mark)

\(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |F(s)|^2 ds = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{2}{\pi} \frac{1}{(1+s^2)^2} ds = \frac{4}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Equate: } 1 = \frac{4}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(1+s^2)^2} ds\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2} = \frac{\pi}{4}.\)

(1 Mark)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
Parseval's identity: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |F(s)|^2 ds\)(4)
where \(F(s) = \mathcal{F}\{f(x)\} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) e^{isx} dx\)(3)
Interpretation: Energy in time domain = Energy in frequency domain(2)
Generalization: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) \overline{g(x)} dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} F(s) \overline{G(s)} ds\)(3)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier transform.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
Let \(f(x) = e^{-|x|}\), then \(F(s) = \mathcal{F}\{e^{-|x|\}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{1+s^2}\)(3)
Parseval's identity: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x)|^2 dx = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |F(s)|^2 ds\)(2)
LHS: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-2|x|} dx = 2\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-2x} dx = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 1\)(3)
RHS: \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{1+s^2} \right)^2 ds = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2}\)(3)
Thus \(1 = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2}\)(2)
Therefore \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{ds}{(1+s^2)^2} = \frac{\pi}{2}\)(2)
